subject: Hosted evaluation: rapid onramp eligibility and rate bands
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@novapricing.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2024 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted evaluation: quick follow-up

Jordan — thanks for the demo earlier. Lina and I walked through the session notes and we wanted to confirm a few practical items so we can decide whether to start with a hosted trial or push for a dedicated proof-of-concept. Quick bullets from our side:

- Primary ask: latency under 250ms tail for single-turn queries (50–200 tokens).
- Traffic profile: mix of high-velocity chat (peak 120rps for short prompts) + batch embedding jobs overnight.
- Data residency: most users in US, but concern about EU customers later.
- Compliance: SOC 2 report and basic audit logs required.

Can you confirm whether hosted API supports burst to 120rps for the chat endpoints out of the box, or whether we need a dedicated capacity baseline first? Also, would you be able to share a simple list of endpoints and their default concurrency/ratebands for the hosted quickstart? We can attach a small sample of our daily traffic distribution.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up.

— Samir
Director of Integrations, NovaPricing
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@novapricing.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2024 16:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quick follow-up

Samir — great questions, thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: hosted can often support bursts without upfront Dedicated capacity procurement; we provide skewed ratebands and short-term burst allowances for quickstarts. That said, for sustained 120rps at low tail latency you may hit throttles unless we provision a higher rate slice.

I attached a one-pager outlining the hosted quickstart endpoints and typical default caps. High-level:
- /v1/chat/completions (streaming): default slice 30–60 rps, burst policy can allow short windows up to ~150rps depending on token mix.
- /v1/embeddings: default concurrent batch limit 8 jobs; overnight batches are handled separately and we can advise on staging policies.
- Concurrency is influenced by prompt length and KV cache behavior.

Next steps I recommend:
1) You share the traffic sample (CSV) — we’ll model requested SLOs against median token lengths.
2) We’ll propose a hosted quickstart slice with recommended ratebands and an ops playbook (prefetch/KV cache hints).
3) If sustained throughput is required, we can propose a Dedicated baseline with committed capacity pricing.

Proposed 30-min ops call: Fri Aug 16, 10:00–10:30am ET or Mon Aug 19, 2:00–2:30pm ET. I’ve CC’d Marissa (solutions lead) who can advise on initial rateband config.

Attachment: hosted-quickstart-endpoints.pdf (see stub)

— Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Rao <samir@novapricing.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@novapricing.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2024 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quick follow-up

Thanks Jordan — attaching the traffic sample (evaluation-traffic-sample.csv). A couple clarifications after Lina reviewed:

- The 120rps number is a short daily peak (5–10 minutes). The 99th percentile latency requirement is firm for customer-facing flows.
- For embeddings we can tolerate background windowing. Cost is a consideration — if hosted gets us to parity on unit cost with moderate tuning we’d prefer to stay hosted.
- Compliance: we do need SOC 2 evidence and a basic audit-log export. Is SOC 2 covered on hosted accounts or only on Dedicated/Private?

If hosted can give us a two-week proof with a higher burst allowance and access to audit logs, that's ideal. Otherwise we may need to discuss Dedicated capacity options.

— Samir

Attachments: evaluation-traffic-sample.csv (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@novapricing.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2024 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quick follow-up

Samir — thanks for the CSV, that helps. Quick technical clarifications from an ops perspective:

- Hosted bursts: we can enable a short-term elevated burst window for a hosted trial (typical window 10–20 minutes) to cover the 120rps peaks. For sustained peaks we recommend a reserved slice via Dedicated.
- 99p latency: achievable on hosted for most prompt sizes if we set a higher ephemeral slice and tune batching/cache. We'll run a simple model with your CSV and return expected tail latency numbers by EOD Monday.
- SOC 2 & logs: SOC 2 is available for Redwood's hosted product; we can provide the report and an audit-log export (queryable) for evaluation purposes. For production-grade audit/retention SLAs we offer private/VPC options + longer retention as add-ons.

I attached a short SLA draft showing retention buckets and options (SLA-draft-Redwood.pdf). Two quick asks for the modeling exercise:
1) Confirm average prompt+response token length for chat (or send sample prompts).
2) Share a preferred time for the ops call (Jordan proposed Fri 10am ET or Mon 2pm ET).

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP):
- Today: Send prompt length sample (NovaPricing) — Samir
- Mon (EOD): Redwood returns modeled tail latency and proposed hosted slice — Marissa
- Tue: Ops call to agree on quickstart slice and schedule sandbox access — Jordan + Marissa

Happy to run this with you — if the modeled latency looks off we’ll pivot to a Dedicated proposal with committed throughput numbers and pricing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-draft-Redwood.pdf (stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@novapricing.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Aug 2024 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quick follow-up

Samir — looping back after Marissa's notes. We're aligned on the MAP and can run the model once you share a representative set of prompt/response pairs. Quick logistics:

- I’ll provision a sandbox token scoped to a hosted quickstart slice after the ops call. The sandbox includes endpoint URLs and example rateband settings.
- If you want to trial immediately we can enable a 14-day hosted burst window (ops-controlled) while we validate tail latencies; no commitment required.
- If post-trial the sustained 99p is not met, we’ll provide a Dedicated baseline that maps to your observed token mix/throughput and an Ops migration plan.

Proposed ops call times (pick one):
- Mon Aug 19, 14:00–14:30 ET
- Tue Aug 20, 11:00–11:30 ET

Can you (a) confirm a slot and (b) drop 4–6 sample prompts with expected response lengths? I’ll send the calendar invite and the sandbox link once we lock the time.

Thanks — Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
